issues.legal_issue: Article 14 does not entitle a person whose land is acquired to the same exemption as another person if that other person’s exemption was unlawful.
material_facts: The landowners challenged the acquisition as discriminatory because several other industrial units had been exempted.
The exempted units had constructed factory buildings and begun manufacturing; the appellants had taken no tangible steps to erect factory buildings or begin production.
One exempted unit’s construction, alleged to be unlawful, had been regularized.
issues.conclusion: Even if the exemptions granted to the other units were erroneous or illegal, the appellants had no right under Article 14 to receive the same relief; granting it would perpetuate a wrong.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not require repetition of an unlawful act as a form of equal treatment; equal treatment presupposes a similar legal foothold. The Court applied Union of India v. International Trading Co. and Anr.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A person challenges the acquisition of their land.
predicates.exemption_claim_based_on_comparator: The person claims exemption by relying on another landholder who was exempted from acquisition.
predicates.comparator_exemption_was_illegal: The other landholder’s exemption was unlawful or unjustified.

issues.definition: When a person challenging a land acquisition relies on another landholder’s unlawful exemption, that comparison does not give the person a right to the same exemption.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not substitute its judgment for the responsible authority’s assessment of whether exempting land would undermine a planned development scheme.
material_facts: The acquisition was for a planned phase of an industrial estate, and the appellants’ land lay between existing phases.
The authorities considered whether the land could be exempted without jeopardizing the development scheme and concluded that leaving it out would disrupt planned development.
Unlike units whose exemptions were recommended, the appellants had taken no tangible steps to erect factory buildings or commence industrial production.
issues.conclusion: The authorities’ assessment that exempting the appellants’ land would jeopardize planned development was not a basis for judicial interference, and the appellants had no ground to require exemption.
issues.legal_principle: The authority responsible for implementing planned development is best placed to assess which land can be exempted without jeopardizing the scheme. Whether to exempt land because construction has been carried out is a matter of policy, and courts do not sit in appeal over the responsible authority’s satisfaction. The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 permits acquisition of land and structures on it.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and acquisition_serves_planned_development and responsible_authority_assessed_exemption_effect and exemption_would_disrupt_development

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A person challenges the acquisition of their land.
predicates.acquisition_serves_planned_development: The acquisition is intended to carry out a planned development scheme.
predicates.responsible_authority_assessed_exemption: The authority responsible for implementing the scheme assessed whether the land could be exempted.
predicates.exemption_would_disrupt_development: Exempting the land would jeopardize or disrupt the planned development.

issues.definition: Where a responsible authority assesses that exempting land acquired for planned development would disrupt the scheme, a court does not interfere with the acquisition merely because exemption is sought.

issues.legal_issue: A representation by an official that permission to change land use would follow a gift of land does not make a later acquisition by the State illegal.
material_facts: The landowners gave strips of land to a local body for widening a passage after a planning official represented that permission to change the land use would be granted.
The State later included their land in an acquisition for an industrial estate.
The landowners relied on the representation to argue that the State was estopped from acquiring their land.
issues.conclusion: The representation was not enforceable against the State so as to invalidate the acquisition; the landowners could seek to challenge the gifts, but that did not make the acquisition proceedings illegal.
issues.legal_principle: A representation by the Director of Town and Country Planning concerning permission to change land use could not be enforced against the State to prevent acquisition. A possible challenge to the gifts for failure to fulfil the commitment does not invalidate the acquisition.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A person challenges the acquisition of their land.
predicates.official_made_conditional_land_use_repre: An official represented that permission to change land use would be granted on a stated condition.
predicates.land_was_gifted_in_reliance: The person gave land to a local body in reliance on that representation.

issues.definition: When land is acquired after an official’s conditional land-use representation led the landowner to gift land, the representation does not by itself invalidate the acquisition.
